title: Canonical universal map for localization of the tensor base
statement: Let R, Rp, A, B and D be commutative rings, with compatible maps R to Rp, Rp to A and B, R to A and B, and from A tensor_R B and A tensor_Rp B to D. Let S be a multiplicative submonoid of R with Rp its localization. For any A-complex Q and base-derived tensor cohomology models L over R and K over Rp [def-pc-base-derived-tensor-cohomology-model], define the canonical B-linear map from L cohomology to K cohomology by the following universal lift. Exact restriction of scalars induces T:D(Rp) to D(R). Compose the factorization of T on homotopy categories, the counit of L, and the ordinary localization tensor identification to obtain a counit for T composed with L. Lift it uniquely to K using its universal counit. Identify the restricted inputs and conjugate its degree-i cohomology map by the two model cohomology isomorphisms. A D-linear map is characterized when it sends 1 tensor x to 1 tensor the canonical B-linear image of x. This generator condition determines it uniquely.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary tensor NatIso using compatible scalar actions. Exact restriction descends to derived categories. Form the counit composite and its universal lift using leftDerivedLift. Identify inputs by restriction composition and the two factorization isomorphisms, then apply cohomology. Extension-of-scalars hom_ext proves uniqueness of the characterized D-linear morphism.
